title: tier-2 shipped code: the mover command words against BuildMoverPhysicsCommand (0x140cb74a0)
notes: SHIPPED-CODE tier-2 unit. The candidate is crates/ow-sim/src/movement.rs, called by crates/ow-sim/src/bin/verify_probe.rs through the build_mover_command entry.
Oracle is BuildMoverPhysicsCommand at exe 0x140cb74a0 (v2b 0x7ff7c59d74a0), extent 0x140cb74a0..0x140cb760d (365 bytes); the unit declares coverageWindow 365.

The builder calls the movement gate FUN_140ca7d80 (0x140ca7d80) first. The fixture pins body+0x698 (the gate's record count) to zero, so the gate returns body[0x1a78] != 0 && body[0x658] != 0 and never enters its indirect record loop; the probe refuses a positive count instead of guessing it.

The first word is selected by +0x1a7b, +0x1a75 and +0x1a60. The action word starts at 0x10a1 when the obfuscated state test passes or +0x652 is zero; otherwise it is 0x14a1 or 0x14b9, then the 0xfff7/0xffef masks and the 0x1a7f clear. The tail word is +0x23c. The function writes six bytes; the unit's out is eight bytes and the last two stay at the fixture's 0xCC.

The two obfuscated byte tests are pinned at their exact boundaries: (state_1a79 + 0x59) ^ 0x71 == 0xEC is state_1a79 0x44, and rotr(byte_1a7a,1)+0x4d rotated left == 0xC5 is byte_1a7a 0x2B. Neighbours are in the first cases so the mutation stage can see them.
Call site: MoverStateMachine (0x140cbacc0) calls ApplyStateModifiers then SubmitMoverPhysicsCommand (0x140cc03d0), which calls this builder before SetCharacterControllerVelocity.

knownEquivalentMutants.rationale: Line 207 is `let second = if ((b.wrapping_add(0x14) >> 1) == 0 && (b & 1) == 0) || !s.flag_652 {`. This is the shift-amount boundary mutant (`>> 1` becomes `>> 0`), the one the mutator's decimal rule reaches first on the line. The branch is taken exactly when b == 0xEC: `(b + 0x14) mod 256 >> 1 == 0` leaves b in {0xEC, 0xED}, and the `& 1` test drops the odd one. With `>> 0` the first test is `b + 0x14 == 0`, which is b == 0xEC alone, and 0xEC is even, so the second test still passes. Both spellings select the same b for every one of the 256 state bytes, and no other input reaches the term. What would observe a difference: nothing in this unit - the branch's only other input is `s.flag_652`, which the mutation does not touch.

Line 207, the hex-constant boundary mutant (0x14 becomes 0x15). The branch is taken exactly when b == 0xEC (see the `>> 0` sibling above). With 0x15 the first test leaves b in {0xEB, 0xEC}, and the `& 1` test drops the odd one, so the branch still selects b == 0xEC. What would observe a difference: nothing in this unit. The sibling boundary mutants on the same line are NOT equivalent and are deliberately left undeclared: `>> 2` widens the first test to b in {0xEC..0xEF} (so 0xEE also takes the branch) and 0x13 moves it to {0xED, 0xEE} (so 0xEE takes it). Those two are probed and killed.

Line 207, `& 1` widened to `& 3`. The second test is only reached with b in {0xEC, 0xED}, where `b & 3` is 0 for 0xEC and 1 for 0xED - the same two answers `b & 1` gives, because 0xEC and 0xED differ only in bit 0. So the widened mask yields the same boolean for every u8 b. What would observe a difference: a b whose bit 1 is set while bit 0 is clear, which the first test cannot reach.

acknowledgedGaps: The unit proves the command words given the gate result. The gate itself (FUN_140ca7d80), its record loop and its indirect [record+0x28]->[vtable+0x78] call are not modelled; the fixture keeps the record count at zero. The callers and the Domino dispatch remain open.
